item.text:
**Do not accept both slices yet.** The page now opens the fortnight library, but the code still displays inferred scores for undirected ranges and leaves another composite path able to use them.

- **Theme chart lanes contradict the design.** For a five-range theme, the adapter assigns scores from −2 to +2 in stored low-to-high order; `laneOf` then looks those scores up in the opposite order. I checked the functions directly: stored positions 1–5 produce lanes **4, 3, 2, 1, 0**. The chart’s axis also prints the inferred score, such as `−2`, even though the card chip shows the range without a score. The design calls for lanes by position and no investment-score wording. [adapter](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/adapters/bundle.js:46), [lane selection](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/model/thesis.js:39), [axis rendering](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/components/primitives.js:24)

- **The trial composite bypasses the new guard.** `prepareIdeaComposite` refuses an undirected driver, but the exported `prepareCompositeTrial` reaches the same numerical history calculation without that check. A two-choice event or theme range can therefore still contribute an inferred number through that path. Guard both entry points and test that the affected driver is named and no score or reweighted result is produced. [composite.js](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/idea/composite.js:107), [trial path](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/idea/composite.js:187)

- **A three-choice `unrecorded` question still fails the dataset.** The design says a view without a ladder row in a clean store shows its stored labels by position. The contract permits three choices only when `answerShape` is `event`; an unrecorded three-choice view is refused. The mixed-store test should include that shape, not only a two- or five-choice view. [contract.js](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/model/contract.js:86), [design](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/page-contract/DESIGN.md:29)

There is also a presentation mismatch: the undirected table has an “Answer definitions” heading, but its enclosing disclosure still says “Score definitions.” [thesis-detail.js](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/components/thesis-detail.js:296)

The saved evidence supports the narrower result that the **12-question fortnight page validated and the headless probe saw the reported chips and D397 section**. It was not a person’s browser review, as the result correctly says. The saved mutant summary reports failures, but does not include their tracebacks; I did not rerun the write-producing checks in this read-only review. [RESULT.md](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/page-contract/RESULT.md:10), [mutants.txt](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/page-contract/mutants.txt)

**Next step:** fix and prove these page-contract defects in the same integration slice, then repeat the real-page check—including the chart axis, an unrecorded three-choice question and both composite entry points. The D397 display can be recorded as built with its observed page result, but the combined slice should await that proof.

CONSENSUS: no, because undirected chart and composite paths still invent or expose scores, and an unrecorded three-choice question still blocks the page.
